notes:
Short background: Kilohertz builds live multiplayer game services that include NPC dialog, matchmaker messages, and personalized recommendations. Very latency- and cost-sensitive: player-facing text must appear in <40ms on average and tail p99 should be under ~120ms for short responses. Huge volume variability (evening peaks) — need autoscale + predictable unit economics.

POC focus: show that Redwood Dedicated + Optimize can match or beat in-house Triton setup on throughput and cost while giving simpler rollouts and observability. Priority features: smart batching, prefix/KV caching, quantization guidance (int8/llm.int8-ish), and perf benchmarking hooks. Team explicitly asked for: "automated batching suggestions and a simple cache policy that doesn't break context correctness."

Baseline vs POC highlights (notes from perf deck):
- Baseline (in-house Triton; 8xA100, batch=1): p50 token latency ~10–14ms, p95 ~46–58ms, observed p99 spikes at 180–240ms during bursts.
- Redwood Dedicated w/continuous batching and prefix cache (batch windows tuned): p50 ~8–12ms, p95 ~18–28ms, p99 mostly <110ms after tuning.
- Cost: Redwood's ded. config with quantized 16/8-bit kernels showed ~30–40% reduction in token compute cost vs baseline; further ~10–15% savings from effective prefix cache hit rates (POC simulated ~25% hit).
- Notes on quantization: customer willing to accept small quality delta for int8 on non-critical system prompts (recommend A/B test for key prompts). They requested Redwood to provide model artifact recommendations (quant config per model family).

Security & deployment: VPC peering required, customer-managed KMS preferred, US-East data residency requested for now. SOC2 + ISO27001 are must-haves for procurement; they added audit_log retention requirement (12 months).

Org signals: engineering lead (CTO Alex Romero) is technically hands-on; infra lead wants to see reproducible benchmarking harness (they requested Jupyter + CSV runs). Budget conversation: procurement prefers annual reserved capacity but wants an initial 3-month ramp and a usage cap.

Sales notes / soft quotes: estimated ARR range $75k–$250k depending on reserved capacity and observability add-ons. Customer loves Redwood Console demo (traces + token cost breakouts) but asked for deeper per-route breakdowns and per-prompt regressions.

Next steps (detailed):
- Redwood to deliver final POC perf report with raw CSVs + recommended batching/quant profiles (due 2026-03-14).
- Legal to share DPA draft; Kilohertz legal to confirm KMS terms.
- Architect session: schedule 90-min runbook review to map autoscale policies and fallback routing (target week of 2026-03-22).

Customer quotes / paraphrases: "If you can give us predictable p99s and a clear path to reduce token spend, we can move to reserved capacity in Q2."

Open questions for SE: exact mechanism Redwood uses for KV cache invalidation across model rollouts; ability to pin model quantization per-route; fine-grained cost attribution down to prompt templates.
